topic: Sharp generated-donor-proxy minimax frontier for realized-path causal buy-and-hold level wealth. Fix H, proxy dimension p and finitely many cohorts; observe N donor scores and n_s replicated untreated wealth blocks across T pre-event windows, with conditional cross-unit independence, geometric temporal beta-mixing, bounded wealth, stable Holder(lambda) proxy-coordinate regressions, interior event-path overlap, limited anticipation and no spillovers. Use the full uniformly elliptic conditional covariance of the stacked donor-error path. At each realized event path impose a two-sided covariance-standardized local modulus with kappa=min(lambda,1). Determine sharp conditional MSE and uniformly honest expected-length rates across arbitrary N,T,n_s growth, the exact oracle/generated-proxy phase diagram, an attaining replicated-donor cross-fitted local-polynomial or tensor-sieve estimator with calendar-block inference, and matching Le Cam/Assouad bounds. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: In the scalar H=0, one-cohort Gaussian-donor subexperiment, event locations O(N^-1/2) apart have bounded KL; affine or asymmetric-cusp regressions satisfying the corrected modulus separate targets by O(N^-kappa/2), yielding MSE N^-kappa and honest-length N^-kappa/2 lower bounds, matched by known-regression plug-in. Checks excluded constant-regression, noiseless temporal-contrast, cohort-cancellation, and identified prior-art collisions; the combined four-term rate remains heuristic and unproved. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove one feasible estimator and conditionally honest interval attain the maximum of treated-mean noise, replicated-response smoothing, random-design spacing, and proxy-modulus terms under unknown heteroscedastic donor laws and overlapping beta-mixing windows, with matching lower bounds in every relative-growth regime and no extra deconvolution or logarithmic phase. EARLY KILL TEST: In scalar iid H=0 with lambda=kappa<=1, bounded responses, T latent design points, n response replicates, and N donor replicates, prove MSE max{n^-1,(Tn)^(-2lambda/(2lambda+1)),T^(-2lambda),N^-lambda} and the square-root honest-length rate; pivot if noisy training covariates force any larger term.

open_problems.open_problem: In the scalar iid H=0 experiment, determine whether generated donor information produces only an N^(-lambda) MSE term or instead turns the training design into an errors-in-variables inverse problem with a slower deconvolution term.

source_refs.claim: Generated-covariate kernel regression admits stochastic expansions and asymptotic distributions, but the analysis is not a uniform minimax result over arbitrary first- and second-stage sample-size ratios.
source_refs.author: Enno Mammen, Christoph Rothe, Melanie Schienle

source_refs.claim: Replicated covariate measurements can recover known-error deconvolution performance, providing the adverse benchmark if every training coordinate is classically contaminated.
source_refs.author: Aurore Delaigle, Peter Hall, Alexander Meister

source_refs.claim: Local-linear regression has pointwise and integrated minimax properties under fixed and random designs, furnishing the oracle-regression benchmark.
source_refs.author: Jianqing Fan

Sample splitting removes own-observation dependence but does not control boundary crossings of the indicator

open_problems.why_unsolved: The key unresolved distinction is sigma-field level: one cross-fitted donor estimate may perturb only the evaluation location by N^(-1/2), in which case Holder stability yields N^(-lambda) squared loss, whereas noise attached to all T training coordinates creates an inverse problem. Generated-regressor expansions are mainly differentiability-based local asymptotics, replicated-measurement papers assume classical per-observation contamination, and the prior proposals show that sample splitting alone does not stabilize moving neighborhoods. The missing first step is a conditional perturbation lemma that preserves the local-polynomial Gram matrix when the center, but not the training design, is generated.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient characterization of the observed sigma-fields together with matching conditional MSE and honest-length bounds for max{n^(-1),(Tn)^(-2lambda/(2lambda+1)),T^(-2lambda),N^(-lambda)}, or an explicit admissible noisy-training-covariate submodel yielding the correct slower deconvolution rate.

writing_exemplar.why: Its framing cleanly separates generation of the covariate from the final nonparametric regression and makes the first-stage effect the central question.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: a covariate is estimated before regression -> generated locations perturb smoothing neighborhoods -> ordinary oracle asymptotics need correction -> determine whether this nonregular Holder target incurs only a modulus loss or a deconvolution loss

method_exemplars.technique: Use random-design local-linear bias and variance bounds, then replace Taylor linearization of the generated center by a conditional Holder perturbation inequality.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the oracle estimator and pointwise minimax benchmark to which the generated-center experiment must be compared.

method_exemplars.technique: Embed a repeated-measurement errors-in-variables experiment and compare its convolution operator with the sigma-field generated by cross-fitted donor scores.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It decides the early-kill branch: if the proposed data really contain noisy training covariates, its inverse-problem machinery identifies the missing phase.

open_problems.open_problem: For fixed path dimension d, derive the exact oracle/generated-proxy phase diagram among treated-cohort noise, replicated-response smoothing, random-design spacing, and donor-proxy uncertainty, including whether d=p or d=p(H+1) and whether tensor-Gram noise creates a fifth phase.

source_refs.claim: The foundational d-dimensional Holder regression rate is sample_size^(-2lambda/(2lambda+d)) under regular random design.
source_refs.author: Charles J. Stone

source_refs.claim: Local-polynomial regression adapts to design and boundary geometry and is asymptotically minimax efficient among linear smoothers, including multivariate local-linear estimation.
source_refs.author: Jianqing Fan, Theo Gasser, Irene Gijbels, Michael Brockmann, Joachim Engel
source_refs.venue: Annals of the Institute of Statistical Mathematics

source_refs.claim: Sharp pointwise rates vary with local random-design mass, so fill distance can remain first order after replication suppresses response noise.
source_refs.author: Stephane Gaiffas

source_refs.claim: Synthetic-control consistency under joint growth of donor count and pretreatment periods does not provide a nonparametric replicated-response and generated-location minimax phase diagram.
source_refs.author: Bruno Ferman
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.excerpt: localization replaces n by roughly n h^d and makes the basis itself bandwidth dependent
empirical scalar-mass bounds must become uniform lower-eigenvalue bounds for two random local-polynomial Gram matrices
individual projectors and labels are discontinuous although their cluster sum is stable

open_problems.why_unsolved: Classical smoothing balances response noise and bias at a fixed point, while many-donor synthetic-control asymptotics balance N and T through factor reconstruction. Here replication can drive stochastic error below the T-point fill-distance error, a generated event location contributes N^(-kappa), and the effective dimension changes if the stacked H+1 path is unrestricted rather than coordinate- or tensor-structured. Prior CausalSmith runs further show that local mass does not automatically imply polynomial Gram coercivity and that data-dependent regime selection cannot be conditioned on a discontinuous preliminary event.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A same-class upper-and-lower characterization, conditional first on realized design geometry, that gives the risk as the maximum of the cohort-weighted treated variance, the d-dimensional replicated-smoothing term, the fill-distance term, and N^(-kappa), states every pairwise boundary and oracle threshold N approximately R_oracle^(-1/kappa), and adds or rules out a separate tensor-Gram phase.

writing_exemplar.why: Its simultaneous many-period and many-control organization is a useful template for presenting mutually exclusive growth regimes and their interpretation.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: donor and pretreatment dimensions may grow together -> distinct ratios support distinct approximations -> no single asymptotic ordering covers all data sets -> map the oracle and generated-proxy regions across arbitrary N,T,n_s growth

method_exemplars.technique: Use multivariate local-polynomial moment matrices and tensor-product bias expansions, with the bandwidth clipped below by realized path-space fill distance.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired upper bound is an oracle local-polynomial risk proof with two new perturbations: a generated center and replicated observations at each design site.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt d-dimensional Holder bump packings to replicated sites and separate random-hole events from response-noise alternatives.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the minimax smoothing exponent against which the proposed four-channel phase diagram must be calibrated.

open_problems.open_problem: Formulate and estimate a feasible two-sided covariance-standardized local modulus for scalar realized-path wealth that uses the full unknown stacked donor-error covariance without imposing an impossible co-Holder condition in every direction when d>1.

source_refs.claim: Minimax estimation of linear functionals in Gaussian experiments is governed by a modulus of continuity and can be attained up to sharp constants by affine procedures.
source_refs.author: David L. Donoho

source_refs.claim: Ordered moduli yield finite-sample optimal and asymptotically honest inference for linear functionals over convex regression classes.
source_refs.author: Timothy B. Armstrong, Michal Kolesar

source_refs.claim: Estimated regressors contribute influence-function terms both as conditioning variables and as arguments of later nonparametric regressions, but this differentiable theory does not cover a kappa-cusp target.
source_refs.author: Jinyong Hahn, Geert Ridder

source_refs.excerpt: aggregate the exact Proposition A.4 coefficients first, derive the full staircase covariance
marginal intervals or diagonal covariance therefore omit both within-label outcome noise and cross-label dependence

open_problems.why_unsolved: For kappa<1 the location effect is nonregular, so an influence correction does not exhaust first-stage risk. Estimating and whitening the full covariance can rotate the least-favorable direction, and covariance error must remain negligible even when N is the bottleneck. More basically, a scalar regression cannot obey a uniform lower Holder inequality along every direction in an open multidimensional neighborhood. The web modulus literature suggests an ordered class modulus or least-favorable cone, while prior panel proposals show that covariance must be calculated only after shared primitive donor and treated-cell coefficients are aggregated.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A well-posed conditional parameter class with an upper Holder stability condition and a lower attainable ordered modulus in the Mahalanobis metric, plus a cross-fitted covariance estimator and perturbation bound showing whether covariance estimation changes only constants or creates an additional phase.

writing_exemplar.why: Its exposition separates the function class, ordered modulus, estimator, and honest interval, which is exactly the clarification this opportunity needs.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: uniform inference requires a precise parameter class -> the class induces an ordered modulus -> the modulus selects least-favorable directions and bias -> replace Euclidean geometry by the full donor-path covariance geometry

method_exemplars.technique: Optimize a conditional modulus over admissible path perturbations and construct the corresponding near-optimal affine or localized estimator.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The target's N^(-kappa) difficulty is asserted through a local modulus, so optimal-recovery geometry directly defines both the least-favorable pair and the attaining center.

method_exemplars.technique: Cross-fit the covariance and generated regressor, then bound their effect as arguments of the second-stage regression without differentiating the cusp component.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It isolates the two roles of a generated regressor that must be retained, while the new proof replaces its smooth linearization exactly where kappa<1 makes it invalid.

open_problems.open_problem: Construct a calendar-block, full-covariance confidence interval for realized-path buy-and-hold level wealth that is conditionally honest under overlapping geometrically beta-mixing windows and has expected length equal to the square root of the active minimax phase without an extra logarithmic factor.

source_refs.claim: Bias-aware local-polynomial procedures yield simple honest and nearly efficient fixed-length intervals by accounting explicitly for worst-case smoothing bias.
source_refs.author: Timothy B. Armstrong, Michal Kolesar

source_refs.claim: Moving-block bootstrap and jackknife methods consistently approximate statistics of stationary dependent sequences under diverging but sublinear block length.
source_refs.author: Hans R. Kunsch

source_refs.claim: Synthetic-control prediction intervals separate uncertainty from weight estimation and post-treatment innovations, but not nonregular generated-location bias under overlapping windows.
source_refs.author: Matias D. Cattaneo, Yingjie Feng, Rocio Titiunik
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.excerpt: simultaneous control of n-dependent spline complexity, reconstruction noise, causal nuisance products
the necessity frontier for an uninflated multiplier band remains open

open_problems.why_unsolved: Bias-aware nonparametric intervals are mainly proved for independent or fixed designs, block methods handle dependence for approximately linear statistics, and synthetic-control intervals do not combine generated locations with minimax smoothing and spacing bias. Overlapping calendar windows also make naive cross-fitting leak shared observations. Prior proposals identify the same gap between a sufficient inflated band and a necessity frontier. The missing first step is a conditional Bahadur expansion after jointly choosing donor folds, calendar blocks, and mixing gaps so every coupling and leakage remainder is below whichever of N,T,n_s is active.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A total interval algorithm with separated calendar-block cross-fitting, heteroscedastic full-covariance studentization, and explicit smoothing, spacing, and proxy-modulus bias radii, accompanied by conditional uniform coverage and matching expected-length bounds in every relative-growth regime.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation decomposes uncertainty into interpretable sources before assembling a conditional interval, a useful structure for the four-phase setting.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: counterfactual prediction uses estimated donor weights -> estimation and post-event innovations create distinct uncertainty -> conditional coverage must account for both -> add smoothing, spacing, and nonregular proxy uncertainty under calendar dependence

method_exemplars.technique: Center at a local-polynomial estimate and add the worst-case Holder smoothing and generated-location bias to a covariance-aware stochastic radius.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It directly targets uniform coverage and near-minimax expected length when smoothing bias is first order rather than negligible.

method_exemplars.technique: Use separated moving calendar blocks and a block variance or multiplier approximation after deriving the fold-conditional linear representation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Calendar overlap creates stationary short-range dependence for which block resampling is the natural approximation, but it must be integrated with cross-fitting and bias awareness.

open_problems.open_problem: Construct regime-complete Le Cam and Assouad lower bounds that separately force treated-mean noise, replicated-response smoothing, random-design spacing, and covariance-standardized proxy uncertainty inside one admissible causal wealth class without constant-regression, noiseless-contrast, cohort-cancellation, or invalid-cusp shortcuts.

source_refs.claim: Testing inequalities yield lower bounds on the expected length of confidence intervals with uniform coverage and expose nonadaptation over nested smoothness classes.
source_refs.author: Mark G. Low

source_refs.claim: Moduli of continuity translate statistically indistinguishable alternatives into minimax estimation lower bounds in Gaussian experiments.
source_refs.author: David L. Donoho

source_refs.claim: Holder bump packings provide the classical multivariate nonparametric regression lower-bound mechanism.
source_refs.author: Charles J. Stone

source_refs.excerpt: The exact positive-band minimax exponent, a matching converse, extension beyond the close-pair region
The existing hypothesis-independent channel gives only the product separation
matched lower bounds isolating both an unremoved-tail witness and a local derivative bump

open_problems.why_unsolved: A maximum-of-four upper rate is sharp only if each term is necessary in a subexperiment contained in the same admissible model for every triangular growth array. The proxy pair must keep KL bounded for N^(-1/2)-separated event locations while an affine or asymmetric cusp produces N^(-kappa) squared target separation and satisfies the corrected modulus; the spacing construction must condition on an empty neighborhood without removing response noise; and the cohort embedding must prohibit cancellation. Prior runs warn that hypothesis-independent auxiliary channels often yield only product separation, while the web lower-bound literature treats these channels separately rather than inside one causal panel experiment.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An explicit embedding table for four legal subexperiments—a parametric cohort-mean pair, a replicated Holder bump hypercube, a random empty-ball experiment, and a Gaussian donor-location pair aligned with the full covariance—plus testing reductions yielding each MSE term and its square-root uniformly honest expected-length lower bound uniformly across regime boundaries.

writing_exemplar.why: Its compact progression from coverage to testing to expected-length lower bounds is the right narrative for the interval converse.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: uniform coverage constrains behavior under nearby laws -> nearby laws can separate the target while remaining hard to test -> one interval must accommodate both -> derive a minimax expected-length lower bound for every active phase

method_exemplars.technique: Construct covariance-standardized two-point alternatives along an attainable ordered-modulus direction and convert their target separation and KL bound into MSE and interval-length converses.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It directly matches the proposed N^(-kappa) proxy channel and prevents an invalid multidirectional cusp from entering the parameter class.

method_exemplars.technique: Use an Assouad hypercube of Holder bumps over populated sites and a separate conditional empty-ball pair for fill-distance error.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The two constructions distinguish replicated smoothing information from random-design spacing, which must appear as separate terms in the claimed frontier.

literature_map:
1. Stone (1982) and Fan (1993) anchor multivariate Holder regression rates and pointwise local-linear minimax efficiency.
2. Fan, Gasser, Gijbels, Brockmann, and Engel (1997) supply design-adaptive local-polynomial and tensor-smoothing machinery.
3. Gaiffas (2007) shows that local random-design mass changes sharp pointwise rates, motivating an explicit spacing or fill-distance term.
4. Pathak, Wainwright, and Xiao (2024) provide a modern random-operator minimax framework, but for elliptical rather than generated-proxy Holder classes.
5. Mammen, Rothe, and Schienle (2012) and Hahn and Ridder (2013) establish generated-regressor expansions and differentiable first-stage variance effects.
6. Delaigle, Hall, and Meister (2008) is the repeated-measurement deconvolution benchmark and therefore the scalar early-kill comparator.
7. Deaner (2018) develops nonparametric proxy controls for panels, including rates and confidence bands, but not the donor-path frontier.
8. Abadie (2021), Ferman (2021), and Ben-Michael, Feller, and Rothstein (2021) cover synthetic-control feasibility, joint donor-period growth, and outcome-model augmentation.
9. Arkhangelsky et al. (2021) provide additive synthetic-DID asymptotics rather than nonlinear realized-path wealth inference.
10. Cattaneo, Feng, and Titiunik (2021) and Chernozhukov, Wuthrich, and Zhu (2021) provide synthetic-control prediction and conformal inference, not minimax expected-length frontiers.
11. Kunsch (1989) and Khismatullina and Vogt (2020) anchor block inference and long-run-variance methods for dependent nonparametric data.
12. Donoho (1994), Low (1997), and Armstrong and Kolesar (2018, 2020) supply modulus, honest-length, and bias-aware inference tools.
13. Mitchell and Stafford (2000) document dependence failures in buy-and-hold abnormal-return inference.
14. Goldsmith-Pinkham and Lyu (2025) modernize causal financial event studies but leave geometric buy-and-hold wealth outside their main linear theory.
